_note: ENCOUNTERS — the P11 format, shaped by slice ruling 4 (2026-08-23): combat is simulated and toggleable, so an encounter collapses to a difficulty-ranked row with an enemy list. The full scripted form exists ONLY for the prologue battles, which are fixed by design and precede the map. Authored 2026-08-25 from ENEMY-REVIEW.md. FORMAT IS PROPOSED, NOT RULED — this is the sketch for review.

format.sliceRow: id · difficulty (an integer rank the battle list is sorted by) · enemies (unit ids with counts) · powerSources (optional: the battle's external pool and any scheduled gains) · terrainHint (optional). Nothing else — ruling 4 means no maps, no scripting for slice battles.
format.prologueBattle: The five fixed battles carry the full shape: setup (placed units by zone), schedule (phase-keyed spawns by edge), loseAfter, retreat, civilians, events. CLOCK RULING 2026-08-23: schedules count PHASES — the word turn never appears in encounter data. Placement is by hex — see format.placement.
format.powerSources: kind: external (pool at battle start) | arrival (one-time +X when a unit enters, stays in the pool after its death) | clock (per-phase or conditional gains live on the unit rows themselves — the Lieutenant's EOT, the Vampire Lord's kills).
format.placement: HEX PLACEMENT, ruled 2026-08-25 (zones were vagueries): at:{col,row} places on that hex; at:{near:{col,row},range:N} deploys anywhere within N of it; at:{oneOf:[{col,row},...]} is a scripted either/or. Board: 16×16, ruled 2026-08-25 — row 0 = enemy edge, row 15 = player edge. NOTE: engine/src/core/hex.ts still says WIDTH=HEIGHT=12; the engine constant needs updating by the engine session — the data leads. The old zone word is kept as `was` for provenance; the hex is authoritative. Multi-unit entries list one hex per unit in `hexes`.
format.scriptedEncounter: id · name · setup (units on the board at the start) · schedule (waves by PHASE, each naming units, counts and where they enter). A THIRD kind, first written 2026-09-02: it has a phase script like a prologue battle but is not one of the five, and it carries no hex placements because none were dictated — the sides are named in prose until it gets a board.

scripted.name: Horrors of the Night

setup.was: far side — hex placement added 2026-09-03 with the far-side ruling

schedule.note: nothing arrives — the quiet phase, and the one where the darkness the Eyeblights left does the work

spawn.was: the opposite side — read as the PLAYER edge, since everything else starts far side (2026-09-03)
the opposite side — the player edge

scripted.intent: The board goes dark faster than the party can cross it. Four Eyeblights strip Vision from range 9 and each one that dies floods ten hexes with darkness — then the things that live in darkness arrive.
scripted.source: Dictated 2026-09-02. PHASE NUMBERING IS A READING: dictated as 'next phase ... in the second phase, or their first end phase, there is nothing ... the next one ... the next one', read as waves at the end of phases 1, 2 (empty), 3 and 4. Say so if the empty phase sits elsewhere. No hex placements were dictated beyond the last wave arriving from the opposite side. | 2026-09-03 RULED: all units start on the FAR SIDE of the board, and the battle starts in darkness — every square dark. Hex placements added on that ruling; "from the opposite side" at phase 4 is therefore read as the PLAYER edge, which surrounds the party. NOTE the consequence: with the whole board already dark, the Eyeblights' on-death darkness flood and the Shadow Sorcerer's Nightfall have nothing to darken unless the party makes light — so those effects become the answer to torches and Reveal, not the source of the dark.

standing.effect: Darkness the battlefield condition, covering the whole map from phase 1 — not the painted layer. Every hex is dark before anything moves.
standing.source: Ruled 2026-09-03: "The units in Horror of the Night start on the far side of the board, and it starts in darkness, so every square is dark."
